literal: Nature having-known, [in] strong assembly mouth they-slip-not, of-word collection who-knew purity they.
translation: Those pure ones who have mastered a multitude of words will not falter in their speech before a formidable assembly, having understood its nature.
modern: சொற்களின் தொகுதியை அறிந்த தூய்மையானவர்கள், அவையின் தன்மையை நன்கு அறிந்து, வல்லவர்கள் நிறைந்த அவையில் பேசும்போது வாய் தவறிப் பேச மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet describes the confidence of well-prepared speakers in a learned assembly. 'சொல்லின் தொகை' (the collection of words) refers to a deep mastery of vocabulary and rhetoric, while 'தூய்மை' (purity) points to their clarity of mind and flawless speech. By understanding the nature ('வகை') of the powerful council ('வல் அவை'), these pure and knowledgeable individuals will never let a wrong word slip from their mouths ('வாய் சோரார்'). The verse emphasizes that true mastery of language prevents faltering even before the most intimidating audiences.
